paper_ratings.evidence_note: UEGAN learns unpaired aesthetic enhancement with GANs and fidelity/quality losses, but does not specifically test low-light perceptual realism or named lighting attributes.
GPP-LLIE directly targets realistic low-light enhancement with perceptual priors, but uses a diffusion/transformer approach and reports paired-data experiments, not an unpaired GAN.
Discusses dynamic video content and memorability prediction challenges, but not narration, emotional audio cues, or educational-video comparisons.
QAGAN supports user-desired image qualities using unpaired GAN learning, but the abstract does not study low-light realism or explicit color/lighting preference alignment.
Addresses video memorability rather than image enhancement, attention mechanisms, or perceptual priors.
Describes a video-memorability benchmark, not an image-enhancement method.
Studies multimodal video memorability prediction, not image enhancement or unpaired training.
QAGAN explicitly uses quality attention in an unpaired GAN to transfer user-desired image characteristics, directly grounding that component of the proposed integration.
Explicitly combines audio gestalt with visual and semantic features for video memorability prediction; the abstract does not report a quantified visual-semantic-only ablation.
Provides short-/long-term video memorability context and an action-rich dataset, but no emotional narration or narrated-versus-non-narrated comparison.
Addresses dynamic video memorability prediction, but does not describe audio gestalt fusion or the requested feature comparison.
Concerns unsupervised image enhancement with GANs, not audio-visual video memorability.
Concerns low-light image enhancement with perceptual priors, not memorability prediction.
Concerns quality-attention image enhancement, not multimodal video memorability.
GPP-LLIE supplies VLM-derived global/local perceptual priors and attention for image enhancement, but does not establish unpaired GAN integration or user adaptation.
Defines video memorability prediction and short-term outcomes, but not audio gestalt fusion or visual-semantic baselines.
Uses auditory features and audio gestalt in video memorability prediction, but does not isolate emotional narration or educational-versus-action-rich video effects.
UEGAN explicitly learns enhancement without paired examples and uses attention plus a VGG feature-domain fidelity loss and adversarial quality loss, grounding fidelity and aesthetics components.

association_checks.evidence_note: All three papers concern video memorability; the audio-gestalt study directly proposes audio/visual/semantic fusion, although a visual-semantic-only improvement is not quantified in the abstract.
The collection studies video memorability, action-rich videos, and auditory features, but none tests emotional cues in educational narration against non-narrated action-rich videos.
These papers concern video memorability, not unpaired image enhancement, quality attention, or perceptual priors.
QAGAN supports unpaired quality attention, UEGAN supports unpaired enhancement and content fidelity, and GPP-LLIE supports perceptual priors; their combination and robustness remain untested.
All three papers focus on image enhancement rather than video memorability or audio gestalt.

Unpaired GAN enhancement, aesthetic/fidelity objectives, and perceptual low-light enhancement are individually represented, but no abstract demonstrates the full proposed low-light, user-preference-aligned unpaired GAN.
